analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new paragraph near lines 508-514 on the excluded shape warmup, the idle calibration session and the MLX pool sweep) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new section near lines 956-989 on shape warmup, startup preload and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env var). No code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims in the docs:
- The warmup uses the same KV and service budgets, foreground lease and idle gate, and publishes no observations or work totals. This is consistent with T-029/T-010 availability expectations and with existing memory-admission invariants. Customer requests still preempt the warmup.
- Startup preload runs before registration, so no consumer traffic (A-001) is involved. The warmup probes use synthetic prompts and artifact-default sampling, so no consumer prompt data is exposed. There is no new cross-tenant surface relative to T-041. The warmup does not train rates and does not populate prefix cache entries per the text, but I could not verify this in code.
- Posture-gate skipping in the preload pass affects only non-measuring work. The doc says the registration gate timeout still bounds the preload.
- The env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP (0 or always) is a local operator knob. It affects performance only and does not touch the trust boundaries in TB-002, TB-003 or TB-011.

Open questions for later review: the implementing code (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup, the preload path) is not in this batch. The claims that it publishes no work totals and does not donate to the SSD prefix cache are unverified. The inference.md patch excerpt is truncated, so the full doc text was not examined; this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. No finding qualifies.
